question: Can you explain to me what is Visual programming?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Defines visual programming as a paradigm that decomposes complex visual tasks into simpler subtasks, each solved with an appropriate vision tool, making the overall problem tractable without end-to-end training.
examples: A complex visual query is split into steps like detect, crop, classify
Breaking a hard visual question into detection then classification makes it tractable

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Explains that a language model interprets the natural language query and, using in-context learning or code generation, produces a Python-like modular program determining which modules to call and in what order.
examples: VisProg uses in-context learning to generate Python-like modular programs
ViperGPT leverages code-generation models to compose subroutines via a provided API

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: States that visual programming avoids task-specific training or finetuning, reusing off-the-shelf pretrained models composed at inference time.
examples: No task-specific training is needed; the system composes existing models at inference time
ViperGPT requires no further training since it composes existing models via generated code

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Describes that the generated program executes line by line, where each line invokes an off-the-shelf vision model, image-processing subroutine, or Python function (e.g., detectors, segmenters), with intermediate results feeding into subsequent steps.
examples: An object detector's output boxes are passed to an attribute classifier downstream
Each program line may call an off-the-shelf vision model, with outputs consumed by later parts of the program

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Cites at least two concrete frameworks from the passages (VisProg, ViperGPT, and/or Socratic Models) as instantiations of the visual programming paradigm.
examples: VisProg demonstrated this on four diverse visual tasks
Socratic Models compose multiple pretrained models zero-shot in a modular framework

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: Notes that the approach yields both a solution and an interpretable rationale, because the explicit program separates perception from reasoning, unlike end-to-end models.
examples: VisProg returns a solution plus a comprehensive, interpretable rationale
Unlike end-to-end models, the program makes the reasoning steps explicit

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Elaborates that Socratic Models compose differently-trained pretrained models (e.g., VLMs on image captions, LLMs on large text corpora including code) via multimodal-informed prompting, exploiting their complementary knowledge zero-shot without finetuning.
examples: VLMs excel at visual data from image captions while LLMs cover text domains like code and spreadsheets
SMs use multimodal-informed prompting so models exchange information zero-shot

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Mentions demonstrated tasks such as compositional VQA, zero-shot reasoning on image pairs, factual knowledge object tagging, language-guided image editing, egocentric video QA, multimodal assistive dialogue, or robot perception.
examples: VisProg was demonstrated on compositional VQA, zero-shot image-pair reasoning, and language-guided image editing
Socratic Models enable egocentric video QA, assistive dialogue, and robot perception

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Conveys that neuro-symbolic, training-free composition expands AI systems to the long tail of complex tasks, and notes the structural characteristic that modules follow a pre-defined sequential plan laid out by the LM's generated program.
examples: Neuro-symbolic approaches easily and effectively expand the scope of AI systems to long-tail tasks
Modules execute according to the plan the LM outlined in the code
